_schema: Methodology parameters. These are committee decisions, not observations — index-methodology-v2.md is the source of truth and every entry cites its section. Observations live in the other files in this directory.

objective.ref: §0.1 — adopted 1.4-1.8 convex. A 2.0+ linear target was considered and rejected: in ounce terms it bleeds through cycles.
objective.beta_basis_note: One of 'regressed' or 'modelled'. §8.3 says modelled delta replaces regression beta entirely; it stays on 'regressed' until nav_model.parameters_adopted is true, and the engine refuses to run if the two disagree. Both numbers are reported on every build so the size of the difference is visible before the switch is made.
objective.min_r2_gold_withdrawn: REMOVED 2026-08-17. Declared 0.6 and read by no code since the methodology was written. It could not have been wired: zero of twelve constituents clear it and the observed range is 0.10-0.29, so enforcing it as written would empty the index. Gold equities do not track gold that tightly at daily frequency — an equity carries mine-specific, balance-sheet and market-beta variance that the metal does not, and the §3 non-synchronous-close problem depresses daily R-squared further. The parameter was wrong, not the universe. R-squared remains REPORTED per name and weighted at portfolio level, as a diagnostic on how much of the weighting denominator is explained variance (see §14 item 7, and the sigma_idio question it feeds).

risk.window_note: regression_window is passed to IBKR as durationStr and is inner-joined on date across the equity, gold and FX calendars. Two years of daily bars balances responsiveness against the noise of an OLS on volatile small caps. It was hardcoded in the engine as '2 Y' while this key was declared as prose; wired 17 Aug 2026.
risk.sigma_idio_note: OPEN — see §14 item 7. sigma_idio is the denominator of every weight, and at R-squared 0.10-0.29 most of what it measures is unexplained variance rather than gold-relative risk. The two names with the lowest R-squared carry the highest sigma_idio and the largest weights. Alternatives are MEASURED on every build and printed by --risk-detail: 'weekly' re-estimates on weekly returns, where the non-synchronous close dissolves instead of being modelled; 'shrunk_daily' pulls each name toward the cohort mean at shrinkage_lambda. Neither ships until the committee picks one.
risk.ref: §7. beta_gold is the §0 mandate constraint and sigma_idio is the weight denominator, so the estimator is a methodology choice, not an implementation detail.
risk.numeraire_note: Regressed against gold in AUD, not USD. The cost base is AUD, so USD gold is the wrong regressor: AUD weakness in a risk-off gold rally is a margin tailwind the USD series does not carry. Requires an AUDUSD daily series; falls back to USD with a loud flag.
risk.dimson_note: Dimson (1979) sum-of-lags, +/- dimson_lags days. NOT optional cosmetics. The ASX closes ~06:00 UTC; the XAUUSD daily bar for the same date closes ~21:00 UTC, so a given gold bar is not priced by the ASX until the NEXT session. Measured 2026-08-17 over 2Y: every one of 17 names showed a higher beta AND higher R-squared against gold at t-1 than against gold at t, with t-2 and t+1 both flat at zero - the exact signature of non-synchronous closes rather than of genuine lead-lag. Regressing contemporaneously splits each response across two bars and halves the estimate: portfolio beta read 0.69 at wtd R-squared 0.07, against a Dimson range of 1.48-2.22 per name. Taking the naive number at face value would have reopened the 1.4-1.8 mandate (see HANDOFF step 4) on an artifact.
risk.contemporaneous_note: beta_contemporaneous is reported alongside for transparency. It is the WRONG number for this universe; it is kept so the size of the correction stays visible rather than buried.

estimation_policy.rule: DERIVE OR FAIL. No field value may be invented.

permitted_provenance.sourced: read from a document, which the field cites by key
permitted_provenance.derived: computed from other SOURCED fields by an arithmetic identity or an explicitly stated formula — e.g. inferred = mr_total - M&I, net_debt = debt - cash, or the midpoint of a range the issuer itself published. The inputs must all be sourced and the formula recorded in the note.
permitted_provenance.bound: a conservative limit that runs AGAINST the name, stated as such. Not an estimate of the true value, a value the true one cannot be worse than.

forbidden: calibrated or cohort-median imputation of a value the issuer has not published
run-rate annualisation or extrapolation of a disclosed period into an undisclosed one
apportioning a multi-year programme across a shorter window by judgement
midpoints of ranges the analyst constructed rather than the issuer published
any figure whose note cannot name the arithmetic that produced it
estimation_policy.on_absence: A field that cannot be sourced or derived stays ABSENT. It is never filled. The engine then does one of two things. For a GATE input, it tests whether the gate outcome is invariant across the full empirical range the cohort reports: invariant means the missing value cannot change the answer, so the name proceeds with a warning; not invariant means the answer is unknown and the name FAILS. For a SCORE input, absence mutes the term, which understates the name and is reported.
estimation_policy.materiality_note: A warning rather than a failure is permitted only where the unresolved input cannot move any final weight by more than materiality_bar_pp. tools/sensitivity.py measures this; it is not asserted.
estimation_policy.why: Written after a session in which invented inputs repeatedly produced confident wrong answers. An A$800m apportionment of Evolution's approved capital was recorded and then withdrawn on the realisation that a judgement call was deciding a binary gate — the same figure at the company's own stated run-rate fails Gate 2 by A$573m. The resource-split imputation had already understated M&I non-reserve ounces by 26-65% per name because it was calibrated on two unrepresentative observations. In both cases an absent value would have been visibly absent; the invented one looked like data. An estimate that is wrong is worse than a gap that is known, because a gap stops the pipeline and an estimate propagates through it.

resource_split_imputation.ref: data/README.md — the single permitted imputation. RECALIBRATED 2026-08-17 on nine observed producer splits (NST 59.8, WGX 56.4, EVN 75.2, GMD 69.0, RMS 73.7, RRL 79.3, VAU 70.3, GGP 54.8, BGL 64.5): median 69.0%, mean 67.0%, range 54.8-79.3%. The prior 58% default was calibrated on only NST and WGX — both at the BOTTOM of the range, because they hold the two largest resource bases and resource maturity runs inversely to size in this cohort. It understated M&I non-reserve ounces by 26-65% per name. A two-point calibration on unrepresentative points is worse than no calibration.
resource_split_imputation.disabled_note: DISABLED 2026-08-17 under estimation_policy. This rule invented mi_non_reserve_moz and inferred_moz from a cohort-calibrated split for any name that published a resource total but not its M/I/Inferred breakdown. It is the archetype of the forbidden pattern: the first calibration used 58% M&I from two observations that both sat at the bottom of the true range, understating M&I non-reserve ounces by 26-65% per name, and since that term is in the weight numerator every affected name was underweighted — invisibly, because the output looked like data. Names lacking the split are now rejected rather than estimated.

gates.duplicate_removed_note: gates.developer_max_funding_gap_of_mcap was deleted 17 Aug 2026. It was a second copy of gate2.developer_max_funding_gap_of_mcap, which is the one §3.1 defines and the only one the engine reads. Two copies of a threshold is a defect waiting to happen: whichever is edited, the other keeps the old value and nothing reports the disagreement.
gates.capacity_note: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-17, previously declared and read by nothing. §4.3: a target position must be buildable within capacity_max_days_advt days at capacity_max_participation of median daily volume. ADVT is shares_out-independent — it is the ASX's own 90-session average volume (companies.json advt_shares_m) priced at the build-time market price. The test is INERT at EUR 1m and the engine reports the AUM at which each name first breaches instead of merely passing everything: a capacity limit that never binds tells you nothing, the AUM at which it binds is the number §4.3 actually estimates.
gates.spread_note: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-17. Gate 3 had never run: producer_max_spread_pct and developer_max_spread_pct had been in this file since the methodology was written and no code read them. The input is the MEDIAN daily time-weighted quoted spread over spread_window of REGULAR TRADING HOURS, from IBKR BID_ASK daily bars, where the bar's open is the session's average bid and its close the average ask. Not a live snapshot: quotes outside continuous trading are wide and stale, and on 17 Aug 2026 the post-close book put Westgold at 2.25% and Northern Star at 0.56% against RTH-averaged figures of 0.205% and 0.055% — an order of magnitude out, enough to fail eight of fourteen names on an artifact. Median rather than mean so one halted or disorderly session cannot decide a gate; p90 is reported alongside and a name that passes on the median while breaching on p90 is flagged STRAINED rather than failed.
gates.spread_calibration_note: OPEN, same shape as the Gate 2 question. Measured 2026-08-17, every name passes with large margin: the widest producer is Ora Banda at 0.453% against a 1.0% cap, and the median producer is at 0.20%. The gate is not binding on this universe. That is arguably correct — these are liquid ASX names and the gate exists to exclude what cannot be traded, not to tilt — but it should be recorded that Gate 3 currently removes nobody. Note also that Rox at 1.353% passes ONLY on the 4.0% developer cap; on the 1.0% producer cap it would fail. If RXL is reclassified as a producer it fails Gate 3 on the same spread, so the sleeve label is doing real work there.

gate2.ref: §3 and §3.1. Binary, never a tilt. One question for producers: does the company reach the other side of a 40% real gold drawdown, applied to a trailing 3-year real average rather than to spot (see anchor_note), without issuing equity? Horizon is 2 years — the 2011-2015 drawdown ran roughly four, but two years is where a balance sheet either holds or does not.
gate2.unhedged_note: The test is run UNHEDGED (§3). Revenue is computed at the stress price on all production and any hedge gain is disregarded. Otherwise a company passes survival on the strength of the very forward sales that penalise it under §6 purity — Catalyst's 30 koz sold at A$6,075 would pay off handsomely in exactly this scenario.
gate2.cost_note: AISC is inflated at cost_inflation_pa, compounding annually over the horizon. Holding it FLAT is also an assumption and it is the optimistic one: in 2013 costs did not fall with the price, which is exactly why so much of the industry went cash-negative. 5% is set below the 8-12% nominal the sector is currently reporting, on the view that some of that is activity-driven and would ease in a downturn.
gate2.capex_note: committed_capex_aud_m counts CONTRACTED, non-deferrable spend only. Discretionary growth capital is deferrable in a drawdown and is excluded — that distinction is the §7.4 committed-versus-deferrable screen. A name that passes with committed capex unsourced is marked PROVISIONAL, because for a survival gate a missing input makes the test easier, not harder.
gate2.anchor_note: RESOLVED 2026-08-17. The drawdown is applied to a trailing anchor_years real average of AUD gold, NOT to spot. Rationale: anchoring a survival gate to spot makes it mechanically weakest exactly when spot is most extended — i.e. when survival risk is highest. At 40% off a A$6,170 spot the stress price was A$3,702 and every producer passed, so the gate filtered nothing. Against a trailing average the effective shock deepens automatically as spot runs ahead of the average, which removes the recalibration treadmill that re-picking a fixed number would recreate next cycle. Past prices are expressed in today's money at anchor_inflation_pa so the anchor is in the same money as the AISC path, which inflates at cost_inflation_pa; setting anchor_inflation_pa to 0 gives the nominal average, which is a LOWER anchor and therefore a harsher test. Falls back to spot, loudly flagged, when no gold history is available.
gate2.superseded_calibration_warning: OPEN: 40% may be too lenient. Spot is A$6,170/oz after a 64% gain in 2025 and +31% year on year; a 40% drawdown lands at A$3,702/oz, roughly where AUD gold traded in 2023. That is a normalisation, not a stress. A gold bear market is also typically risk-on, which strengthens AUD and AMPLIFIES the fall in AUD gold — a 40% USD drawdown could be 50%+ in AUD. At 40% every current producer passes. Committee should consider either raising the threshold or applying it to a trailing average rather than spot. The breaking-point diagnostic is reported per name meanwhile.

constraints.ref: §9.1 — risk-based, not percentage-of-index based. No regulatory cap applies.
constraints.idio_note: ENFORCED 2026-08-17, previously declared and read by nothing. Portfolio idiosyncratic variance is sum of w^2 * sigma^2 — the cross terms vanish because idiosyncratic risks are by construction independent — and no name may contribute more than max_idio_variance_contribution of it. On first measurement Pinnacle contributed 34.1% against the 15% cap, Catalyst 13.2% and Westgold 12.1%; enforcing it roughly halves the top position. That gap between the declared methodology and the shipped index was the largest open one in the build. The cap is feasible only while max_idio_variance_contribution >= 1/n, since an equally-contributing book sits at 1/n each; the engine refuses to run rather than iterate forever if the universe narrows past that point.
constraints.single_asset_note: WIRED 2026-08-17 against companies.json single_asset_shares, which is UNSOURCED for every name — so the constraint runs and reports UNTESTED rather than passing silently. Note what the arithmetic implies: with max_single_name 15% below max_single_asset 20%, a wholly single-asset constituent cannot breach this cap on its own. It can only bind where two or more constituents hold the SAME asset, which no pair in the current universe does. Sourcing the per-asset ounce split is therefore low priority for the cap and high priority for disclosure (§15) — four constituents are single-asset.

nav_model.ref: §8. BUILT 2026-08-17 (nav_model.py). Channel 1 (deck re-rating, P/NAV) is the largest convexity term and every score before this date was a LOWER BOUND driven by Channels 2 and 3 only.
nav_model.adoption_note: parameters_adopted is FALSE and the model therefore does not touch a shipped weight. §14 item 3 requires the committee to publish and defend the discount rates and the conservative deck first, and 5% / 9% real are inherited placeholders that nobody has defended. The model runs on every build regardless and prints the book it WOULD produce beside the book that ships, because a committee cannot sensibly adopt a discount rate without seeing what it does. Setting parameters_adopted true switches Channel 1 into the convexity score and modelled delta into the mandate check, in one move.
nav_model.conservative_deck_note: 'gate2_anchor' means the conservative long-term deck IS the Gate 2 anchor — the trailing 3-year real average of AUD gold, currently A$4,944/oz against a spot of A$6,219. Chosen so that no new number has to be invented and defended: the survival gate and the conservative NAV deck then run off one price, which is already argued in §3 and already recomputed every build. Set conservative_deck to 'fixed' and conservative_deck_aud_oz to a number to override. Committee decision either way.
nav_model.non_reserve_note: 'confidence_weights' values non-reserve material by mining it, not by an in-situ A$/oz. M&I non-reserve and Inferred ounces are converted at the already-adopted §7.2b confidence weights (0.5 and 0.2) and produced AFTER reserves are exhausted, at the same rate and the same AISC. This deliberately avoids inventing an in-situ A$/oz parameter — §8.2 asks for one, and there is no way to set it that is not a judgement call. It also makes gamma emerge rather than be assumed: ounces twenty years out at today's AISC are worth almost nothing at a low gold price and a great deal at a high one, which is precisely the convexity the product exists to hold.
nav_model.gamma_note: delta_bump is the local finite difference for dNAV/dAu; stress_bump is the wide one. LOCAL GAMMA IS IDENTICALLY ZERO IN THIS MODEL AND THAT IS A FINDING. With a fixed mine plan, one AISC and no cut-off-grade response, NAV is exactly A*(deck - AISC) - debt, which is linear in the deck, so every finite difference returns the same delta. It does not mean these companies have no gamma; it means the disclosed data cannot express where their gamma comes from. Real gold-miner convexity is the cut-off grade falling as the price rises — ounces that are waste at A$3,000 and ore at A$6,000 — and measuring it needs the §7.2c grade-tonnage curves the data layer carries for no name. At stress_bump the model does bend, but that curvature is operating and financial leverage, which §0.1 is explicit about NOT wanting to be paid in. The up/down NAV capture reported off stress_bump is §12.2's ratio computed forward instead of backward, which is the one version of it that carries no survivorship or look-ahead bias.
nav_model.limitations_note: Three, all stated rather than papered over. (1) Growth capital and the production it buys are BOTH excluded — the model values the current operation at the current rate on the current cost base. Including committed capex without the ounces it unlocks would penalise every builder in the book, and committed capex is unsourced for five names, so including it would also be inconsistent across the cross-section. (2) The model is gold-only, so it cannot yet produce the forward gold-share-of-NAV that §6.1 asks purity to be measured on: that needs non-gold reserve, grade and price inputs the data layer does not carry. Purity stays on TTM revenue and EVN stays the name that distinction was written for. (3) One production rate and one AISC per company, because that is what is disclosed — no grade profile, no mine schedule, no cost curve. §7.2c cost-curve shape is therefore still unmeasured.

rebalance.event_driven: corporate actions, jurisdictional events, Gate 1 or Gate 2 breaches — never deferred to the next cycle

reporting.ref: §12. In ounce terms the index only rises if it outperforms gold. That is the demanding measure and the right one.
